title: Daily protection rules on 2-year books (per-setup lot caps, realized+open stops, account realized+open stop, correlated-cluster cap): none passes
hypothesis: A daily stop or exposure cap cuts the worst days without lowering total R more than random thinning would.
notes: Books Primary / T1 / T2 / Graveyard x 11 variants (+ as-run baseline). Every book loses on 2 years, so every cap 'improves' total R by trading less; none beats random thinning in both splits on Primary with >= 80% trades kept. Open-risk stops (-3R) cut the worst-5% days by ~75% but keep only 35-49% of trades and lose to random thinning on T2 and the Graveyard. part_b.csv. open two-year history, locked block 2024-11..2025-02 never loaded; TRAIN <= 2025-12, VALID 2026-01..10-07; production + tod costs, extended tier x3; refire chain + lot cap 3 as-run; no holdout scored.
